# Example: a finished BA-Kit project

This folder is a **read-only worked example** so you can see what BA-Kit produces
*before* you run anything yourself. Nothing here is generated by the installer —
it's a hand-curated snapshot of a realistic project after the default workflow
has run.

> New to the framework? Read [Concepts & glossary](../docs/concepts.md) and
> [Getting started](../docs/getting-started.md) first, then come back here to see
> the output.

## What you're looking at

A small project, **Customer Feedback Portal**, with one task that has been taken
through the default flow:

```
ba.analyze-docs  →  ba.specify  →  ba.write-stories
```

```
customer-feedback-portal/
├─ project.md                         # the project brief
├─ kb/
│  └─ index.md                        # shared knowledge base (index-first)
└─ tasks/
   └─ 001-feedback-intake/
      ├─ inputs/
      │  ├─ README.md                 # guidance placed by init-task
      │  └─ stakeholder-brief.md      # the raw material the analyst was given
      └─ artifacts/                   # everything the AI + analyst produced
         ├─ docs-analysis.md          # what was extracted from the inputs
         ├─ requirements.md           # the approved requirements (status: approved)
         └─ user-stories.md           # INVEST stories derived from the requirements
```

## How to read it

1. Start with [`inputs/stakeholder-brief.md`](customer-feedback-portal/tasks/001-feedback-intake/inputs/stakeholder-brief.md)
   — this is the messy, real-world input.
2. See how `ba.analyze-docs` turned it into
   [`docs-analysis.md`](customer-feedback-portal/tasks/001-feedback-intake/artifacts/docs-analysis.md),
   surfacing gaps and open questions instead of guessing.
3. See how `ba.specify` produced the approved
   [`requirements.md`](customer-feedback-portal/tasks/001-feedback-intake/artifacts/requirements.md),
   with every requirement traced back to a source.
4. See how `ba.write-stories` produced
   [`user-stories.md`](customer-feedback-portal/tasks/001-feedback-intake/artifacts/user-stories.md)
   from the **approved** requirements.

Notice the **traceability**: every requirement cites where it came from, and the
stories list the requirement IDs they cover. That chain is the whole point.

## Want to make your own?

Follow [Getting started](../docs/getting-started.md). Your real work lands in a
git-ignored `workspace/` folder, never here.
